result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): Both answers correctly flag the real blocker: the form shows a confirmation but never saves anything. Both also note the missing date and location and the unvalidated name field. A starts by saying what already works, uses clearly marked placeholders instead of facts, and catches the decimal bug, though its replacement submit handler is bigger than a minimal edit. B gives no code, but it lists more extras (what to bring, duplicate submissions, an email field) and states a wrong 'today' date as fact, which makes it less reliable. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): Both answers correctly flag the real blocker: the form never sends data anywhere, so every member would get a false confirmation. A pads the list with extras (what-to-bring list, duplicate handling, an email field) and states an unsupported 'today is Saturday 2026-10-17'. B's handler rewrite is longer than a line or two, but it is targeted and clearly scoped.
